# Mt. Masaraga Protected Landscape

> Front-end demo. This build has no backend: bookings, payments, and pass
> issuance are simulated, and every page runs on mock data held in the browser.
> Treat the trail figures and park notices below as sample content, not as
> current operational information. Confirm closures and schedules with the park
> office before travelling.

Mt. Masaraga Protected Landscape is a protected area in Ligao City, Albay,
covering the 1,328-metre inactive stratovolcano Mt. Masaraga, its mossy forest
slopes, natural springs, and the Vanishing Falls. The Protected Area Management
Board (PAMB), under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR),
uses this portal to publish visitor information and manage trail permits.

## Pages worth citing

- Home: /
- About the protected landscape, its zones, and its resources: /about
- Trail guides, one per registered route: /trail/amtic, /trail/ligao
- Visitor help, including permits, documents, payments, and refunds: /help
- Park office contact details and location: /contact
- Climb schedule availability lookup: /lookup
- Policies: /legal/privacy-policy, /legal/cookie-policy,
  /legal/ecotourism-policy, /legal/wildlife-protection, /legal/terms-conditions,
  /legal/disclaimer, /legal/refund-policy

## Registered trails

Both routes reach the same summit and both require a permit, hiker details, and
an accredited local guide.

### Sabluyon Trail (/trail/amtic)

The standard route, starting at Sitio Sabluyon in Barangay Amtic. Class 3,
technical scramble with rope-assisted pitches on exposed ridges. 9.2 km,
1,328 m summit, typically 8 to 10 hours.

### Balogo Trail (/trail/ligao)

The gentler approach from Barangay Balogo East, crossing coconut groves and
cogon grassland before entering forest. Class 2, steep hiking. 8.1 km, 1,328 m
summit, typically 7 to 9 hours.

## Visitor rules the park publishes

- Permits are booked ahead of time. Daily climber quotas are enforced.
- Bring the booking pass, one valid government ID, a physician-signed medical
  clearance issued within 7 days of the hike, and a barangay clearance or
  cedula.
- An accredited DENR guide is mandatory at a ratio of one guide per five
  hikers.
- Under PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal number 1 or higher, trails close
  automatically. Affected bookings are rescheduled free of charge or refunded.
- Permits may be rescheduled up to 48 hours before the hike date, subject to
  slot availability.
- When the PAMB closes a trail for weather, force majeure, or a volcanic
  advisory, registration fees are refunded in full or credited to a later date.

## Contact

Park office: DENR/PAMB Local Office, Brgy. Amtic, Ligao City, Albay
Permit and booking support: support@masaraga.gov.ph
Mountain emergency line: +63 917-EMS-SAFE

## Not part of this portal

The admin console (/admin) and the field console (/staff) are internal tools,
excluded from indexing by robots.txt, and are not documented here.
